web.how.p1: Votes are counted at each polling unit and the figures are written on a result sheet.
web.how.p2_h: 2. The sheet is displayed and photographed

web.how.p4: It reads the figures from the photo, checks that they add up as the form requires, sends uncertain sheets to a person, and lets people registered to that unit compare the figures with the sheet posted at their unit and report differences.
web.how.p5_h: 5. What this tool does not do
web.how.p5: It does not declare results. Only INEC declares official results. Figures here are unofficial.
web.how.caveat: This is a general description. It must be checked against INEC's published procedures before any real use.
web.about.title: About this proof of concept
web.about.does: Reads handwritten figures from photographed polling-unit result sheets with a model that runs on one local GPU, checks the arithmetic, routes uncertain sheets to people, and lets citizens and accredited observers confirm or dispute what was recorded for their own unit, on the web or on a basic phone (USSD).
web.about.not: It never declares results, never finds anyone guilty of anything (a discrepancy is only a flag for review), never ranks or colours anything by party, and has no link to INEC systems.
web.about.data: Phone numbers only as salted hashes; a self-declared polling-unit code; the figures read from each sheet with a link to the image. No voter cards, registers or biometrics. Real sheets appear only as redacted copies with names, signatures, codes and party names blacked out.
web.about.limits: Self-declared registration cannot prove presence at a unit, so citizen checks are a signal, not proof. Arithmetic checks cannot catch a forgery that keeps every total consistent. Accuracy was measured on a small sample of real sheets.
